newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end slightly down in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end slightly down in thin trade.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares ended slightly down in thin trade on Friday, with many investors retreating from the market amid weak sentiment, brokers said.

The Hong Kong stock market had sucked a lot of foreign investment from the B share market and domestic investors were being cautious in the leadup to 1997 interim reports due to be released by the end of August, they said.
The B index edged down 0.079 points or 0.10 percent to 76.369 points on volume of 9.434 million shares worth $5.459 million.
"Major institutions have left the market and investor sentiment won't revive in the short term," a local broker said.
Selling of electric appliance-related stocks late in the afternoon session depressed the market, but trading was still sluggish with little investor interest, brokers said.
"Some institutional investors sold electric appliance stocks late in the session due to concerns about their results, which helped send the market down," another local broker said.
Sharp competition in the electrical appliance industry is expected to have a negative effect on the interim results of companies in the sector.
Of 45 B shares, 36 traded with 14 down, 13 up and nine flat.
Shanghai Shangling Electric Appliances Co was the biggest loser on talk of poor interim results. It plunged $0.020 or 9.80 percent to $0.184.
Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor Co followed on expectations of poor earnings, slipping $0.024 or 5.66 percent to $0.400.
Hainan Airlines Co was the most actively traded on institutional buying, gaining $0.002 or 0.36 percent to $0.550 on volume of 1.105 million shares.
Shanghai's A shares ended up on light speculative buying, but sentiment was cautious amid market uncertainties, brokers said.
The A index rose 13.599 points or 1.09 percent to 1,265.613 points on volume of 459.386 million shares worth 5.937 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index gained 30.113 points or 0.78 percent to 3,904.582 points.
Brokers said the A and B share markets were likely to continue to trade around current levels as investors waited for fresh news, including the release of more interim results.
